title: Labor Supply among Homeless Street-Paper Sellers: Evidence from a Randomized Wage Increase
abstract: arXiv:2602.11992v3 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: We conduct a pre-registered randomized controlled trial to test for income targeting in labor-supply decisions among sellers of a Swedish street paper. Unlike most workers, these sellers choose their own hours and often face severe liquidity constraints and volatile incomes. Treated individuals received a 25 percent bonus per copy sold via Swish, the mobile payment system that accounts for roughly 80 percent of sales, for the duration of an issue, simulating an increase in earnings potential. Consistent with standard labor-supply theory, they sold more papers and, by our measures, worked longer hours and took fewer days off. These findings contrast with studies on intertemporal labor supply that find small substitution effects.

translated_title: 无家可归的街头报纸销售者的劳动供给：来自随机工资上涨的证据
translated_abstract: 我们进行了一项预先注册的随机对照试验，以检验瑞典街头报纸销售者劳动供给决策中的收入目标行为。与大多数劳动者不同，这些销售者自行选择工作时间，并且经常面临严重的流动性约束和收入波动。在某一期销售期间，接受处理的销售者通过Swish（一种约占销售额80%的移动支付系统）每售出一份报纸可获得25%的奖金，模拟了潜在收益的增加。与标准劳动供给理论一致，他们售出了更多报纸，并且根据我们的测量，工作时间更长，休假天数更少。这些发现与那些发现替代效应较小的跨期劳动供给研究形成了对比。
tldr: 随机对照试验表明，当无家可归的街头报纸销售者获得25%的销售奖金后，他们显著增加了销售量和工作时间并减少了休假，这一结果支持标准劳动供给理论，与发现替代效应较小的跨期劳动供给研究形成对比。
en_tdlr: A randomized controlled trial shows that homeless street-paper sellers who received a 25% bonus per copy sold increased their sales, worked longer hours, and took fewer days off, consistent with standard labor-supply theory and contrasting with studies finding small substitution effects in intertemporal labor supply.
